rules.statement: An appellate court should exercise caution when reviewing the evidence to determine whether a conclusion reached by a trial judge should stand, and should not overturn the trial judge's decision unless the evidence does not support it.
rules.supporting_quote: "If there is no evidence to support a particular conclusion (and this is really a question of law) the appellate court will not hesitate so to decide. But if the evidence as a whole can reasonably be regarded as justifying the conclusion arrived at at the trial, and especially if that conclusion has been arrived at on conflicting testimony by a tribunal which saw and heard the witnesses, the appellate court will bear in mind that it has not enjoyed this opportunity and that the view of the trial judge as to where credibility lies is entitled to great weight."
